claims.text: Room-temperature ion irradiation of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 will generate point defects.
The irradiation-induced point defects will be uniformly distributed.
Irradiation-induced point defects will act as effective magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Controlled ion irradiation will increase the coercive field relative to an unirradiated FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 baseline.
The initial FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy has a largely defect-free crystalline matrix.
The initial FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy has soft-magnetic properties.
The proposed intervention uses approximately 100 keV He+ or Ar+ irradiation at fluences from 10^14 to 10^16 ions/cm².
Dose optimization within the proposed fluence range can create defects without inducing amorphization.
The structural mediator will consist of point defects and small defect clusters within the crystalline matrix.
The introduced defects impede magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion raises the energy barrier for domain-wall movement.
A higher domain-wall-motion barrier increases coercivity.
At an optimal irradiation dose, coercivity will show a dose-dependent increase over the unirradiated baseline.
Excessively high irradiation doses may amorphize the alloy and counteract the magnetic improvement.
Elevated-temperature irradiation may fail to produce the desired coercivity enhancement.
Defect-induced domain-wall pinning is a well-established mechanism.
The optimal irradiation dose and quantitative coercivity increase are unknown until experimentally determined.

contradictions.description: Amorphization and magnetic degradation at excessive dose are presented as an expected boundary of the hypothesis, but the same result is also designated as a falsifier. An anticipated high-dose failure does not falsify the claimed optimal-dose enhancement.

The predicted response is nonmonotonic or limited to an optimal dose range, whereas the falsification rule asks for a systematic increase with increasing fluence. A decline at the highest dose could satisfy the prediction while failing the stated falsification criterion.
